The statement acknowledges that the coronavirus will weigh on activity and elevate downside risks, but it also pairs that shock with an unusually forceful policy response—cutting the funds rate to the effective lower bound, large-scale Treasury and MBS purchases, expanded repo operations and discount-window access, reduced reserve requirements, and coordinated dollar swap lines. Consistent with the credit-channel literature (e.g., bank-lending and external-finance-premium mechanisms documented by Kashyap–Lamont–Stein, Gertler–Gilchrist, and related work), these tools can stabilize funding markets and support investment and household spending, especially for bank-dependent firms. With market-based inflation compensation down and longer-term survey expectations stable, inflation risks are muted; inflation-targeting and credibility research implies ample room to ease without unanchoring expectations. Balance-sheet policies at the zero lower bound also address liquidity-trap constraints by improving market functioning and keeping reserves ample. Net: near-term outlook remains negative, but the aggressive policy mix materially cushions the downside relative to the shock alone.
